title: A Gift for the People's Good

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "From among all the Israelites, I have given the Levites as gifts to Aaron and his sons to do the work at the tent of meeting on behalf of the Israelites and to make atonement for them so that no plague will strike the Israelites when they go near the sanctuary." So Moses, Aaron and the whole Israelite community did with the Levites just as the Lord commanded Moses. - Num 8:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God describes the Levites as "gifts" — given to serve at the tent of meeting on behalf of all the people, and to help protect them as they drew near to God's holy presence. The Levites' service was for the good of the whole community. Through their work, the people could safely worship a holy God.

It is beautiful to think of people who serve God as His gifts to His people. Those who teach, care, lead, and serve in God's family are not just doing a job; they are God's gift to the community, given for everyone's good. When we receive faithful servants of God, we are receiving a gift from His hand.

This should shape how we view both serving and being served. If you serve God's people in any way, remember that God has given you as a gift to them — that is a high and humbling calling. And if you are blessed by others' service, receive it with gratitude as coming from God.

The New Testament echoes this beautifully. Christ Himself gives gifts to His church — people set apart to build up His people (Eph 4:11-12). Every faithful servant is part of God's provision for His family.

And chapter after chapter, we keep meeting that quiet refrain: they did "just as the Lord commanded." Obedience runs through it all. Let us thank God for those He gives to serve us, and let us gladly be His gift to others.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you see faithful servants of God as His gifts to you?
- If you serve, do you realise God has given you as a gift to others?
- How can you receive and give service with gratitude?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for those You have given to serve Your people, and thank You for the privilege of being Your gift to others. Help me to serve gladly. Amen.
